project: its graph, its metadata, and the history that built them. Only the history is stored; the other two are folded from it.
layer: a cross-section of the tree at one block: that block's immediate contents, seen from within.
element: anything the graph holds as an object: a block, a note, a group, a proxy.
block: the base element, and the default: one discrete thing the tree is built from. The only structural element.
note: an element drawn as a card of text.
group: the generic organizational element, local to one layer: a boundary round a set. It organizes without structuring.
proxy: a virtual block standing in for one that lives in another layer, so a relationship can cross a structural boundary.
interface: a block sitting on its parent's frame edge. Also called a port. Derived from having a side.
relationship: a join between exactly two elements. Not an element — placed by its ends, drawn as a line, and joins rather than sits.
field: a named, typed value on an element or a relationship. Never structural.
